newsitem.title: UK: Paul McCartney acts to stop sale of song lyrics.
newsitem.headline: Paul McCartney acts to stop sale of song lyrics.

text.p: Paul McCartney on Thursday defended his decision to take legal action to recover song lyrics he wrote 30 years ago from the widow of the Beatles' former road manager.
McCartney's lawyers have acted to stop the sale of the handwritten lyrics of "With A Little Help From My Friends" from the classic 1967 album "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band".
The song was being sold by Lily Evans, 60, whose husband Mal was the Beatles' road manager and a close friend of Paul for a decade. She had hoped to sell them for 60,000 pounds ($100,000).
Mal died in a shooting accident 21 years ago in Los Angeles and the Beatles gave Lily 5,000 pounds to help her out. But she wants to sell the lyrics to help provide for her old age.
"I don't know why he would want to stop me," Lily told the BBC. "After all, he was good friend of Mal's and if I was in Paul's shoes I would want to be helpful rather than hinder."
McCartney stressed in a statement that neither he nor the Beatles bore any ill will towards Lily, but the lyrics were not her property and she had no right to sell them.

Mal had collected up the song sheet after a recording session and it was returned to his widow with the rest of his personal effects in the "tragic circumstances" surrounding his shooting by Los Angeles police, the statement said.
"It is highly unreasonable for Mrs Evans to claim them as her own property," McCartney said. Mal has his own place in Beatles history as the man who hit the hammer in "Maxwell's Silver Hammer."
The matter has received publicity because Lily Evans' case has been taken up by a BBC television programme.

"The programme is trying to make the Beatles out to be widow-beaters," McCartney said. "I would like to meet with Mrs Evans and discuss this and come to some arrangement to see that she is taken care of and the lyrics are returned."
McCartney, one of the world's mnost successful songwriters, was awarded a knighthood by Queen Elizabeth in this year's New Year's honours list.
